2:83.ar: وَإِذۡ أَخَذۡنَا مِيثَٰقَ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ لَا تَعۡبُدُونَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ وَبِٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ إِحۡسَانࣰ ا وَذِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينِ وَقُولُواْ لِلنَّاسِ حُسۡنࣰ ا وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُواْ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ ثُمَّ تَوَلَّيۡتُمۡ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ ا مِّنكُمۡ وَأَنتُم مُّعۡرِضُونَ
2:83.en: And (remember) when We made a covenant with the Children of Israel, (saying): Worship none save Allah (only), and be good to parents and to kindred and to orphans and the needy, and speak kindly to mankind; and establish worship and pay the poor-due. Then, after that, ye slid back, save a few of you, being averse

4:36.ar: ۞وَٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَلَا تُشۡرِكُواْ بِهِۦ شَيۡـࣰٔ اۖ وَبِٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ إِحۡسَٰنࣰ ا وَبِذِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينِ وَٱلۡجَارِ ذِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡجَارِ ٱلۡجُنُبِ وَٱلصَّاحِبِ بِٱلۡجَنۢبِ وَٱبۡنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَمَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُمۡۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ مَن كَانَ مُخۡتَالࣰ ا فَخُورًا
4:36.en: And serve Allah. Ascribe no thing as partner unto Him. (Show) kindness unto parents, and unto near kindred, and orphans, and the needy, and unto the neighbour who is of kin (unto you) and the neighbour who is not of kin, and the fellow-traveller and the wayfarer and (the slaves) whom your right hands possess. Lo! Allah loveth not such as are proud and boastful

And he cast down the tablets, and he seized his brother by the head, dragging him toward him. He said: Son of my mother! Lo! the folk did judge me weak and almost killed me. Oh, make not mine enemies to triumph over me and place me not among the evil-doers

OfWcJvK5poo.speaker: adnan
OfWcJvK5poo.speaker_note: First-person continuation of his 'Achieving the Outcomes' series; says he has lived in Canada since 2013, arriving in his late twenties; refers to 'rituals last week or two weeks ago'; title names no other speaker.
OfWcJvK5poo.title: Achieving the Outcomes: Revelation to Ethics
OfWcJvK5poo.one_line: Revelation exists to settle the ethical choices observation cannot, and following it must show as tested ethics, not rituals or background.
OfWcJvK5poo.summary: Episode of 'Achieving the Outcomes' on moving from revelation to ethics. He opens with his central diagnosis: the ummah's suffering comes from aimlessness, and after twelve years in London he sees a community whose only agreed goal is building more masajid. The world still runs on the law of the jungle, where the bigger gun makes the rules, and reforming that is one of Islam's outcomes, but today's point is narrower. Observation can teach many things, but some choices, above all whether to play fair or grab what you can, cannot be settled by trial and error, so revelation settles them. He reads Al-Baqarah 2:83 and An-Nisa 4:36-37 as an expanding circle of care, parents, relatives, orphans, the needy, neighbours, travellers and dependants, and insists these are ethical choices, not rituals. A chain of hadith follows: the Prophet was sent to perfect ethics, faith obliges good treatment of guests and neighbours, the best of you have the best akhlaq, the cheat is not one of us, do not betray even the betrayer. He warns that the English word 'character' waters this down; ethics get tested. The straight path we ask for in every prayer means incorruptibility, and rituals exist to keep us on a path that must exist first. The second khutbah tells how the Prophet rebuked Abu Dharr for a racial slur against Bilal despite his immense record, because ethics come before background, colour and deeds.

outline.heading: Opening
'I'm trying' is not enough
outline.gist: No time in our lives has needed this part of the deen more. It is not enough to tell yourself you are trying: what exactly are you trying to achieve as an individual, a community, a country, a nation?

outline.heading: The aimlessness of this ummah
outline.gist: The ummah's suffering comes from a deep lack of objectives. In twelve years in London, his first observation is that the community does not know what it is here for.

outline.heading: The one goal we agree on: more masajid
outline.gist: The only clear shared goal is building and expanding masajid, whether or not they are needed or filled with services; he has stopped pushing back. A purposeful life demands that everything under it, communities included, be purposeful too.

outline.heading: What are Muslims in the West here to do?
outline.gist: That is the question of the series, and everyone must answer it at the personal, communal, national and international level.

outline.heading: The law of the jungle
outline.gist: Events overseas show humanity still lives by whoever has the bigger gun: they make, break and remake the rules, which apply only to the weak. One of Islam's outcomes is to reform humanity away from that law, though bombs still fall on children, now in Syria too. Today's topic is narrower: revelation to ethics.

outline.heading: What observation cannot settle
outline.gist: An observant, critical mind can derive many beneficial rules, but some questions are almost impossible to settle by observation and trial and error. That is where revelation came in with clear statements.

outline.heading: Play fair or grab what you can
outline.gist: Everyone must decide early whether to play fair when others do not, or race to the end and carry off whatever they can. There is no trial and error: once committed, there is no coming back.

outline.heading: Revelation's answer: play fair
outline.gist: Revelation says there is only one correct answer; the option of grabbing does not exist. The covenant taken from Bani Israel begins with worshipping Allah alone, then turns to ethics.

outline.heading: Al-Baqarah 2:83: the expanding circle of care
outline.gist: After tawhid comes care for parents, then relatives whether you like them or not, orphans who lack social support, the needy who lack financial support, and speaking only with excellence, with prayer and zakat; most turned away.

outline.heading: The same covenant for us: ethical choices
outline.gist: Allah gave Muslims the same instruction in An-Nisa: worship Him without partners, then care for your parents. These are ethical choices, not rituals.

outline.heading: Aging parents: 'I was cute, I paid them back'
outline.gist: Once young and strong, do you care for the people who raised you or say it is their problem, that you never asked to be born and repaid them by being a cute child? It is an ethical choice, and so is care for relatives.

outline.heading: Neighbours, travellers, dependants; Allah does not love the arrogant
outline.gist: The circle widens to related and unrelated neighbours, close companions, the traveller and those under your custody. Allah does not love the vain and arrogant, who are stingy and tell others to be stingy.

outline.heading: Sent to perfect good ethics
outline.gist: The Prophet said he was sent exclusively to perfect good ethics. People knew them since Adam and Nuh; he came to perfect them and explain why, and spent his life doing so.

outline.heading: Faith obliges honouring guests and neighbours
outline.gist: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day honours his guest, does not harm his neighbour, and speaks good or stays silent. Revelation came to set ethics straight; if it does not transform yours, what is its point?

outline.heading: Ethics, not 'character'
outline.gist: The best of you are those with the best ethics. The English word 'character' waters it down; ethics and values get tested: are you compassionate and full of integrity, or only when convenient?

outline.heading: The cheat is not one of us, despite fifty Hajj
outline.gist: The closest to him in Jannah are those with the best ethics, and whoever cheats is not one of his group. Being in his group is the only goal; fifty Hajj and Umrah do not help a cheat.

outline.heading: Do not betray the one who betrayed you
outline.gist: Return the trust to whoever entrusted you, and do not betray even the one who betrayed you. The Prophet lived this and held his followers accountable to it.

outline.heading: Equal by birth; only taqwa differs
outline.gist: Every human is born equal; only taqwa distinguishes, and no one can see it, so no one may be arrogant. Yet compassion, integrity, trustworthiness and fairness are its signs.

outline.heading: The straight path is incorruptibility
outline.gist: Twice in every prayer we ask for the straight path, a figure of speech for a life with no corruption in its ethics. Asked to summarise Islam, the Prophet said: say you believe in Allah, then be upright.

outline.heading: Rituals keep you on a path that must exist first
outline.gist: Islam first brought ethics, values and covenants; then prayer to ask Allah to keep you on that path and let you live and die on it. Worship is for staying on the path, but there has to be an identifiable path first.

outline.heading: Interlude
Abu Dharr, the most truthful, lets slip a slur
outline.gist: The Prophet said no one under the sky is more truthful in heart than Abu Dharr, yet in a dispute he implied something about Bilal's racial background, so subtly that bystanders barely caught it. The Prophet did.

outline.heading: Musa's anger was overlooked; this was not
outline.gist: Musa threw down the tablets and seized Harun's beard and Allah said nothing, because of all he had done. Abu Dharr's record did not spare him, because this breached the ethics of humility and equality Islam came to establish.

outline.heading: How much jahiliyyah is still inside us?
outline.gist: The Prophet told him he still had jahiliyyah in him; he asks how many of us carry it unidentified. Abu Dharr put his head on the ground and asked Bilal to step on his neck so he could repent.

outline.heading: No appeal to his record: ethics come first
outline.gist: Bilal would not do it, and they made up. Abu Dharr never pleaded his seniority or service; ethics, principles and values come before background, colour, name, country, money and deeds.

outline.heading: Outro

BXuL7lz8qII.speaker: adnan
BXuL7lz8qII.speaker_note: First-person continuation of his 'Achieving the Outcomes' series ('last week we talked about similarities to unity'); mentions his own weekday duroos drawing seven to twelve people; title names no other speaker.
BXuL7lz8qII.title: Achieving the Outcomes: Individual to Community
BXuL7lz8qII.one_line: A Muslim may not exist solo: belonging to the community is an obligation with duties, and freeloaders are the true enemy of any community.
BXuL7lz8qII.summary: Episode of 'Achieving the Outcomes' on moving from the individual to the community. He sets the Islamic view against the social contract tradition of Rousseau and Hobbes: humanity only progressed once it learned to belong to groups, and Islam has a unique version of that contract. The bottom line, stated early, is that a Muslim is not permitted to exist solo; you belong at least to a community, then a nation, the ummah, humanity and finally all creation. Allah commanded the Prophet with five things beginning with jama'ah, and even salah, the most intimate act, is commanded in congregation. Belonging means obligations, not just perks: the hadith of the two-deck ship shows that we sail together or sink together, and leaving the jama'ah is described in frightening terms. Jumuah itself is the weekly community meeting where someone thinks for the group. The verse from Surah Hud he opened with grounds the warning: nations were destroyed when no one was left carrying the group's weight. In the second khutbah he names two hindrances: selfishness, which will be repaid in kind, and nifaq, pictured through the roughly 700 munafiqun of Medina who showed up for spoils but not for battle. Freeloading, he says, is what makes a free Palestine less likely, and he asks each listener to audit themselves as Umar did.

outline.heading: Opening
From individual to community: the social contract
outline.gist: Unlike last week's move from similarity to unity, today is about the individual and the group. Philosophers spent centuries on the social contract because humanity could not escape war and famine until it learned to belong, and modern citizenship rests on Rousseau and Hobbes.

outline.heading: Gaza and a narrative growing more aggressive
outline.gist: Muslims have their own understanding of belonging, and losing it is part of why almost two years of killing and starvation in Gaza continue, with the oppressors now speaking openly of occupying the area and expelling everyone.

outline.heading: Never again, and the Muslim record
outline.gist: Humanity thought ethnic cleansing was over. Muslims always knew it was wrong and left conquered peoples with their temples and books, which is why the Muslim world is so diverse and why that diversity is now used against it.

outline.heading: The bottom line: no Muslim may fly solo
outline.gist: A Muslim is seen and valued as an individual only within the group he belongs to. Existing solo is not an option: a Muslim belongs at least to a community.

outline.heading: The ladder of belonging
outline.gist: Understanding Islam moves you up from individual to community, nation, ummah, humanity and finally all creation. Feeling at one with everything Allah made is the endgame, not the starting point.

outline.heading: Jama'ah first, even in salah
outline.gist: In a long hadith the Prophet said his Lord commanded him with five things, the first being jama'ah. Even salah, the most intimate conversation with Allah, is commanded in congregation.

outline.heading: The Islamic social contract: no perks without weight
outline.gist: Congregation does not strip individuality: you feed and protect the community and it protects your individuality and creativity. Claiming to belong while wanting only the benefits is not how the contract works.

outline.heading: The hadith of the two-deck ship
outline.gist: Two groups draw lots for the decks; those below decide to drill a hole for water rather than trouble those above. If the upper deck stops them all sail, and if it leaves them all sink.

outline.heading: Sail together or sink: no rowboat
outline.gist: There is no private rowboat in the middle of the ocean. The end-times flight to the mountains with one's family and sheep is nowhere near while hundreds of millions of like-minded Muslims surround you.

outline.heading: Never leave the jama'ah, even a broken one
outline.gist: Whoever leaves the jama'ah even a hand's span takes off the cloak of Islam. You belong for better or worse, wronged or not, and a broken system is more reason to contribute.

outline.heading: Why Jumuah is obligatory
outline.gist: His weekday lessons draw seven to twelve people, yet Jumuah fills because Allah made it obligatory. Everyone in an area must meet weekly so someone thinks for the group and says what comes next: the most important hour of the week.

outline.heading: Bilal and the outliers the group carried
outline.gist: The group made people like Bilal equals, protected and fed them, and they poured their wealth, time and energy back into it. Before Allah we exist only as part of something, starting with the local community.

outline.heading: The nations destroyed when no one carried the weight
outline.gist: The verse from Surah Hud he opened with: earlier nations were taken because no one was left advocating for the group's future. They shared one land but had become selfish individuals, except the few Allah saved.

outline.heading: Interlude
Belonging made the early generation selfless
outline.gist: Poor, hungry and oppressed, they broke their insufficient bread for others because the Prophet had turned individuals into a group. Loving those stories is easy; living them starts with belonging to family and community before humanity.

outline.heading: Against individualism: lift what is falling
outline.gist: Western individualism is getting worse, focused only on what I want. Seeing what is missing and putting your shoulder under it, unasked and unpaid, only happens if you feel part of the community.

outline.heading: First hindrance: selfishness
outline.gist: If you are too selfish to care, a day will come, even in this world, when you need people and they do not care about you. What goes around comes around.

outline.heading: Second hindrance: nifaq as freeloading
outline.gist: Around 700 munafiqun lived in Medina, perhaps a third of the city, appearing for free food and handouts but never when asked to carry something. Today the same people want fatwas, funerals and marriage services and give nothing back.

outline.heading: Freeloaders, the true enemy of community
outline.gist: He judges their behaviour, not their hearts: they came for the spoils and stayed back from battle. They are the hardest part of running a community, and the more of them there are, the less likely Gaza eats or Palestine is freed.

outline.heading: Self-audit: am I that person?
outline.gist: Ask as Umar asked whether he was on the list of hypocrites: am I only here for the good times, or contributing? Holding ourselves to that standard brings better outcomes.

outline.heading: Outro

eBmEdPHLHMM.title: Achieving the Outcomes: Similarities to Unity
eBmEdPHLHMM.one_line: Muslims are ridiculously similar yet not united; disunity is what allowed Gaza, and unity must start locally by deflating egos.
eBmEdPHLHMM.summary: Episode of 'Achieving the Outcomes' on unity, a subject he has preached a dozen times and will keep raising until it changes. The outcome Allah wanted and the Prophet achieved was unity, and the ummah is not moving toward it. He grounds this in Aal Imran 3:102-105 (hold the rope of Allah together; He united the hearts of enemies; do not divide like those before you) and Al-Anfal 8:46 (dispute and your momentum departs). He states with certainty that any degree of unity would have prevented what has happened to Gaza, because the oppressors learned that Muslims will not stand together even on what they all agree on. He is unimpressed by Canada's conditional recognition of a Palestinian state after starvation and tells Muslims to be impressed by nothing short of full acknowledgement, and to shed the fear that comes from standing alone. Muslims are ridiculously similar and need unity on only a few issues, Palestine the obvious first. Start locally: London's Muslims operate in silos, and a city of 40,000 that cannot unite should not expect nations to. The second khutbah names the barriers, arrogance, envy, victim mentality and egos, prays with Al-Anfal 8:63 for hearts to be joined again, and points to the 27 nationalities in the room as the material of unity.

outline.heading: Opening
A topic he will not move on from
outline.gist: He has preached unity about a dozen times from different angles and will keep at it until Muslims in the West and in small cities see some resolution; moving on from an unaddressed priority would be unwise.

outline.heading: What are we trying to turn into?
outline.gist: What did the Prophet want for us and achieve? No sane person thinks the status quo is good. We need not invent the answers: Allah made clear what He wants, and the Prophet achieved it.

outline.heading: On this one, we are not moving
outline.gist: Other things may be improving, but on this outcome we are absolutely not moving forward. In the middle of Aal Imran, Allah teaches how to preserve the nation, beginning with the verse heard at every Jumuah: be mindful of Allah as He deserves.

outline.heading: Hold on to the rope, all together
outline.gist: The rope is a figure for the lifeline thrown to someone drowning: hold on to it for dear life, all of you together, and do not divide.

outline.heading: Enemies at the edge of the fire; do not divide
outline.gist: Remember that you were enemies on the brink of the fire and He joined your hearts. Do not be like those who divided and fought after clarity came to them; obey Allah and His Messenger and do not dispute, or you will fail.

outline.heading: Any degree of unity would have prevented it
outline.gist: Dispute and the winds that bring baraka stop blowing. He says with certainty that with any degree of unity, the last two years in Gaza would not have happened; the oppressors tested our waters and saw us fight over every detail.

outline.heading: Two billion who agree on ninety percent
outline.gist: He shares the planet with two billion people he agrees with on over ninety percent of life's big questions, yet they cannot line up on something as simple as brothers and sisters being oppressed and land being taken.

outline.heading: Not impressed by Canada's conditional recognition
outline.gist: It took the starvation of a people for the government to consider conditionally accepting a Palestinian state. He is not impressed: they know Muslims will settle for any small win and an excuse to celebrate.

outline.heading: Nothing short of full acknowledgement
outline.gist: No Western government gesture should impress a Muslim unless it fully acknowledges the atrocities against Palestinians in the holy land to this day; complacency is why token actions are thrown our way.

outline.heading: Standing alone breeds fear
outline.gist: Had the starving children looked different, the response would have been different from the start, which shows his value to the government he voted for. Muslims must state their stances clearly; fear comes from standing alone, and the world feels colder and darker when you do.

outline.heading: Ridiculously similar
outline.gist: With two, five, ten people beside you, courage returns. Muslims from Africa, Asia, Eastern Europe and converts share the big questions and grand understandings of the world; if those similarities never become unity, what is the point?

outline.heading: Skeletons wrapped in cloth
outline.gist: Children's skeletons are wrapped in cloth and buried with food less than two kilometres away; some are so starved that even food would bring refeeding syndrome and the need for ICUs. Of every topic in the series, this is the cause: similar but not united.

outline.heading: A few issues suffice, and Palestine is the first
outline.gist: You need not agree with the person beside you on everything, but if Palestine is not an issue to unite on, what is? The Prophet was never a force of division.

outline.heading: The shepherd who kept the flock together
outline.gist: As a shepherd boy he learned to keep wandering sheep together, and as a leader he brought back whoever strayed, uniting people with little in common. We are a millionfold more similar than the companions were, yet cannot take a stand.

outline.heading: Start locally; the wolf takes the lone sheep
outline.gist: Unite within cities, stop fighting over trivial issues and debates best left to scholars, and build strength, because unity is strength: the wolf only eats the sheep that is alone.

outline.heading: London's silos
outline.gist: In a small city like London, Muslim groups work in silos with no communication or collaboration while their youth struggle. If 40,000 people cannot unite, how can nations around the holy land be expected to?

outline.heading: Clean our own backyard first; we lack only unity
outline.gist: Make the bed and clean the room first. A united Muslim community in the West has political, social and financial weight and can shift the narrative; we lack no expertise, youth, wealth or passion, only unity.

outline.heading: Interlude
Room for our bodies, not our egos
outline.gist: The barriers to unity have always been arrogance, envy and a victim mentality. The masjid has room for all our bodies but not all our egos; the bubbles have to be popped.

outline.heading: Same jersey, different number
outline.gist: As long as we envy Muslims who do well instead of supporting them and see each other as the other side of the tracks, we go nowhere. Everyone wears the same jersey; if you cannot see it, the problem is your lens.

outline.heading: Only Allah joins hearts
outline.gist: We are ridiculously similar but not united. Allah told the Prophet that spending all the world's wealth could not have joined their hearts, but He joined them; he prays for our hearts to be joined again and for egos not to stand between them.

outline.heading: Twenty-seven nationalities
outline.gist: He counted at least 27 nationalities walking through the door: a special place, a special act, a special group. Realise it and work toward the outcome.

outline.heading: Outro

ZQE_0i3pH6w.title: Tazkiyah Halaqah: Self-Honesty, Episode 11 (Q&A)
ZQE_0i3pH6w.one_line: Questions on self-honesty: the raw self in prayer, addiction and professional help, repeated sins and conviction, practical muhasabah, and anxiety.
ZQE_0i3pH6w.summary: In a question-and-answer session closing the self-honesty module, the sheikh explains that tazkiyah aims at better prayer, and that khushu is largely self-honesty, since self-deception dulls real emotion. He clarifies the raw self: having many roles is good and fulfils being a khalifah, but one must not become a role. We speak to Allah as His servant, not as parent or professional, just as the Prophet was a husband, not a prophet, with Aisha, ate like a servant, and called his followers companions. He warns that these sessions do not cure addiction or mental illness, which need professional help. For a sin one cannot leave, he first asks whether it is an addiction; if not, the real issue is weak conviction that it is wrong, which knowledge must build, as his own reluctance to wear masks during COVID ended only when a colleague nearly died. For muhasabah he advises starting with simple behaviours rather than the need for validation, and using everyday luxuries as bargaining chips, since withholding a privilege is easier than adding work. On anxiety-driven habits he recommends identifying triggers and asking honestly why one is anxious, down to accepting death.

outline.heading: Opening
Everything in Islam is interconnected
outline.gist: Focusing on the current topic often helps a separate struggle, because every aspect of being Muslim improves or worsens together.

outline.heading: Self-honesty is the gateway to khushu
outline.gist: Tazkiyah aims at better salah; lying to oneself breeds shame that dulls real emotion, so khushu is essentially self-honesty.

outline.heading: Many roles, one person beneath
outline.gist: Carrying many roles is good and fulfils being a khalifah; the task is recognising who performs them.

outline.heading: Speaking to Allah as His servant
outline.gist: Defining yourself by a favourite role risks collapse when it is lost; before Allah you stand only as an abd.

outline.heading: Each role worn by the same self
outline.gist: Roles are granted by Allah; a father who parents like a business manager or a president who comes home as president fails at the role.

outline.heading: The Prophet at home and at the table
outline.gist: With Aisha he was a husband, not a prophet issuing commands, and he embraced eating like a servant when mocked for it.

outline.heading: Companions, not followers
outline.gist: Though leader and prophet, he called his followers companions, and Allah honours him most by calling him His servant.

outline.heading: When the roles are taken away
outline.gist: Stranded alone or after losing a job, family or country, those who became their role fall into depression, like retired celebrities.

outline.heading: Who comes out of the grave
outline.gist: You are resurrected with only your name and parents' names, so become comfortable with that person now.

outline.heading: Question: addiction and mental health
outline.gist: These sessions help but do not cure addiction or mental illness; seek professional help, and some exercises need a stable starting point.

outline.heading: Question: repenting but falling back
outline.gist: First identify whether the sin is an addiction, which needs outside support such as rehab and support groups.

outline.heading: Without conviction a sin never stops
outline.gist: If you do not truly believe it is wrong, study who forbade it and why; without conviction you will carry it to the grave.

outline.heading: Tawbah depends on belief
outline.gist: Like workplace rules you disagree with, fear only works short term; lasting change needs agreement that the rule is right.

outline.heading: Wearing masks during COVID
outline.gist: He resented wearing masks all day until a colleague who removed his nearly died; conviction changed his behaviour.

outline.heading: Learning from others' endings
outline.gist: Some mistakes have no return, so the Quran shows the fate of those who disobeyed to build conviction without experience.

outline.heading: Do you believe Allah's rules are good?
outline.gist: Finding you think you know better than Allah on one rule exposes arrogance, which is where real work begins.

outline.heading: Question: muhasabah on seeking attention
outline.gist: Craving validation is too complex to start with; it needs self-value and sincerity first, so begin with a simple behaviour like temper.

outline.heading: Luxuries as bargaining chips
outline.gist: Withhold an evening show, treat or game whenever the sin happens, and within weeks the ego stops pushing.

outline.heading: Withhold a privilege rather than add work
outline.gist: Adding extra work often goes undone and collapses the system; deprivation is simpler to keep.

outline.heading: The ego is trained like a child
outline.gist: Self-honesty reasons with the self and deprivation disciplines it, as consistent salah turns from struggle into enjoyment.

outline.heading: Question: habits driven by anxiety
outline.gist: Get professional help, and also identify triggers and prepare for them, as a parent prepares a jealous four-year-old for a new baby's visit.

outline.heading: Asking why you are anxious
outline.gist: Keep asking 'so what?' to uncover what you overvalue; even facing a terminal diagnosis, everyone dies, so ask whether you are prepared.

outline.heading: Treat roots and symptoms together
outline.gist: Combine honest questioning of causes with practical accountability rather than only masking symptoms.

outline.heading: Outro

WKOw4uzocjI.title: Intellectual Development and Learning Disorders: Facts and Warning Signs
WKOw4uzocjI.one_line: A child psychiatrist explains developmental milestones, psychoeducational testing, IQ cutoffs, learning disorders and ADHD, then discusses misdiagnosis, screens and post-COVID challenges.
WKOw4uzocjI.summary: A child psychiatrist gives a community health session at the masjid. She explains that a child's development must be judged against normal milestone windows and their own trajectory: a late walker within range or a slower talker in a bilingual home is not alarming, while regression after normal development points to an organic cause. She walks through the full psychoeducational assessment, combining school achievement tests, the WISC-V IQ test and caregiver interviews on adaptive functioning. An IQ below 70 indicates intellectual developmental disorder, 70 to 79 is borderline, and a learning disorder requires normal intelligence with a specific deficit in reading, writing or math, as in dyslexia. Using a sample report she shows how percentiles reveal global versus specific deficits, how ADHD compounds learning disorders, and how accommodations such as typing or dictation software can bypass a weakness. Behaviour such as throwing things may be a learned escape from tasks the child cannot do. In questions she discusses misdiagnosis amid shrinking services after COVID, handheld devices shortening attention, self-diagnosed autism, refugee children and selective mutism, and urges parents to advocate for a second opinion.

59:7.ar: مَّآ أَفَآءَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ رَسُولِهِۦ مِنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡقُرَىٰ فَلِلَّهِ وَلِلرَّسُولِ وَلِذِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينِ وَٱبۡنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ كَيۡ لَا يَكُونَ دُولَةَۢ بَيۡنَ ٱلۡأَغۡنِيَآءِ مِنكُمۡۚ وَمَآ ءَاتَىٰكُمُ ٱلرَّسُولُ فَخُذُوهُ وَمَا نَهَىٰكُمۡ عَنۡهُ فَٱنتَهُواْۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
59:7.en: That which Allah giveth as spoil unto His messenger from the people of the townships, it is for Allah and His messenger and for the near of kin and the orphans and the needy and the wayfarer, that it become not a commodity between the rich among you. And whatsoever the messenger giveth you, take it. And whatsoever he forbiddeth, abstain (from it). And keep your duty to Allah. Lo! Allah is stern in reprisal

59:6.ar: وَمَآ أَفَآءَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ رَسُولِهِۦ مِنۡهُمۡ فَمَآ أَوۡجَفۡتُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ مِنۡ خَيۡلࣲ وَلَا رِكَابࣲ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُسَلِّطُ رُسُلَهُۥ عَلَىٰ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
59:6.en: And that which Allah gave as spoil unto His messenger from them, ye urged not any horse or riding-camel for the sake thereof, but Allah giveth His messenger lordship over whom He will. Allah is Able to do all things

ugwON0WPu50.speaker: adnan
ugwON0WPu50.speaker_note: First-person continuation of his 'Achieving the Outcomes' series; refers to his own lecture series 'Intellectual Fellowship of the Prophet' in English and Arabic and to fear for the mosque's charity status; title names no other speaker.
ugwON0WPu50.title: Achieving the Outcomes: Sunnah to Mindset
ugwON0WPu50.one_line: The neglected core of the Sunnah is building strength and standing against oppression; follow the Prophet's letter and his objectives together, as a mindset.
ugwON0WPu50.summary: Episode of 'Achieving the Outcomes', delivered in a mix of English and Arabic, on turning the Sunnah into a mindset. He opens with Al-Hashr 59:7, then admits it is becoming hard to preach while children in Gaza starve; after never avoiding the news since October 2023 he can no longer watch malnourished infants, and he says plainly that the Israeli governments are committing genocide while he fears for the mosque's charity status. The cause, he argues, is a neglected core of the Sunnah: the Prophet understood that the world respects strength and unity, not moral appeals, and worked his whole life to build strength. Muslims are therefore obligated to build academic, financial, social and political strength, and the Prophet would not be impressed by beards and hems while brothers starve. Nothing outranks following him, because only a living example turns a book of values into practice. He illustrates with the three men who vowed extreme worship and the Banu Nadir distribution that provoked grumbling until 59:7 settled it. The Arabic second khutbah ranks the Sunnah's priorities, standing for truth and against oppression above siwak and dress, and warns against two extremes: rejecting the Sunnah altogether and cherry-picking its gentleness. Literal and purposive following must be combined. The question worth studying is how one man became three continents in thirty years.

outline.heading: Opening
Starving children: he can no longer watch
outline.gist: He opens with 'whatever the Messenger gives you, take it', then admits it is ever harder to stand and speak while children starve. He never avoided the news since October 2023 but now cannot watch malnourished infants in emergency departments, with food minutes away.

outline.heading: Genocide while the world negotiates
outline.gist: The food is held back by the most vicious, ethicless army on the planet. The Israeli governments are not attempting genocide but committing it, starving civilians and blaming them, while negotiators trade proposals.

outline.heading: Why: a neglected core of the Sunnah
outline.gist: People starving in one of the most resourceful regions is impossible on its own. It happens because Muslims neglect a main aspect of the Sunnah: not first the outward details he still follows, but the Prophet's understanding that the world respects strength.

outline.heading: The world respects the strong and the united
outline.gist: Appeals to ethics, compassion and the philosophical superiority of the Book have been our failed strategy for years. It has always been this way, and it is why Gaza's children are carried malnourished to their graves.

outline.heading: Commanded to build strength in every domain
outline.gist: The strong make and enforce the rules, which are applied to the weak. Muslims are obligated beyond any other obligation to build academic, intellectual, financial, social and political strength.

outline.heading: He would not be impressed by beards and hems
outline.gist: Do you think the Prophet would praise us for our prayers, siwak and beard length while our brothers starve and we do nothing about our weakness? He would not.

outline.heading: He spent his life telling people to stand up to oppression
outline.gist: He taught people to defend, speak up and even die for justice. Nothing comes remotely close in importance to following him.

outline.heading: A book of values needs a living translator
outline.gist: We cannot take a book of values, principles and ethics and work out its practice ourselves; we need someone who shows how to apply each value in every circumstance.

outline.heading: Whoever turns from my Sunnah is not of me
outline.gist: One man vowed never to marry, another never to stop fasting, another never to sleep at night. The Prophet said he marries, eats reasonable meals and sleeps: building a family and staying functional is his way.

outline.heading: Banu Nadir: wealth not circulated among the rich
outline.gist: When Banu Nadir left their land without combat, Arab custom gave such spoils to the warriors. Al-Hashr assigned it instead to Allah and the Messenger, relatives, orphans, the needy and travellers, so wealth would not circulate only among the rich.

outline.heading: They grumbled; take what the Messenger gives
outline.gist: Some who had waited through the siege were unhappy with the ruling, and the verse answered them: whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids, stop.

outline.heading: Turn his Sunnah into a mindset
outline.gist: His lecture series 'Intellectual Fellowship of the Prophet' is for the young. A great teacher teaches how to think, not only what to do, and the Prophet taught both.

outline.heading: Study how he built strength and refused division
outline.gist: Study him deeply: how he approached problems, built strength and unity and refused disunity, so that what is happening cannot continue.

outline.heading: Young people: not on my watch
outline.gist: The young must look at their future and say this will not happen when they are our age. His generation failed; they can do better.

outline.heading: The path to revival: his Sunnah ranked as he ranked it
outline.gist: The ummah's revival lies in truly holding to his Sunnah as he wanted it held, with its priorities ordered as he ordered them.

outline.heading: Siwak and beard are sunnah, but not the highest
outline.gist: Siwak, voluntary prayers, white garments and the beard are sunnahs but not the highest. Higher are standing with truth, resisting oppression, guarding the ummah's unity and strength, and the Book's ethics of honesty, trust and justice.

outline.heading: Erasing the Sunnah is collective suicide
outline.gist: One extreme denies the Sunnah and its books entirely; without a living example of how he applied Allah's words, the Quran cannot be understood or practised. The other extreme follows him badly, choosing what suits them.

outline.heading: Cherry-picking his gentleness; letter and objectives together
outline.gist: He was merciful and gentle, and elsewhere brave, outspoken and standing against oppression; people pick the gentleness that suits them. He encourages no violence: the truth is to combine following his letter, in dress, food and manner, with pursuing his objectives.

outline.heading: His dreams: a woman travelling safely, charity with no takers
outline.gist: He longed for the day a woman would travel from al-Hirah to Hajj fearing no one but Allah, and a man would go out with charity and find no one to take it. Return to the Sunnah as he would want if he were here.

outline.heading: Otherwise we circle in place
outline.gist: Without this we drive in circles for the rest of our lives. He taught how to adapt, respond, and be proactive and reactive at once.

outline.heading: Two negative approaches
outline.gist: Ignoring the Sunnah altogether is communal suicide; following only its literal details is the other error. Dress and eat like him, and also learn what he aspired to and where he was taking life.

outline.heading: From one man on a mountain to three continents
outline.gist: One man running down a mountain, then his wife, a ten-year-old and a friend; thirty years later the faith spanned three continents. How he did it must be your first interest, before counting rak'ahs, so his example becomes the mindset that guides your choices.

outline.heading: Outro

30:40.ar: ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكُمۡ ثُمَّ رَزَقَكُمۡ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمۡ ثُمَّ يُحۡيِيكُمۡۖ هَلۡ مِن شُرَكَآئِكُم مَّن يَفۡعَلُ مِن ذَٰلِكُم مِّن شَيۡءࣲۚ سُبۡحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ
30:40.en: Allah is He Who created you and then sustained you, then causeth you to die, then giveth life to you again. Is there any of your (so-called) partners (of Allah) that doeth aught of that? Praised and Exalted be He above what they associate (with Him)

30:41.ar: ظَهَرَ ٱلۡفَسَادُ فِي ٱلۡبَرِّ وَٱلۡبَحۡرِ بِمَا كَسَبَتۡ أَيۡدِي ٱلنَّاسِ لِيُذِيقَهُم بَعۡضَ ٱلَّذِي عَمِلُواْ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡجِعُونَ
30:41.en: Corruption doth appear on land and sea because of (the evil) which men's hands have done, that He may make them taste a part of that which they have done, in order that they may return

30:42.ar: قُلۡ سِيرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَٱنظُرُواْ كَيۡفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلُۚ كَانَ أَكۡثَرُهُم مُّشۡرِكِينَ
30:42.en: Say (O Muhammad, to the disbelievers): Travel in the land, and see the nature of the consequence for those who were before you! Most of them were idolaters

30:43.ar: فَأَقِمۡ وَجۡهَكَ لِلدِّينِ ٱلۡقَيِّمِ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن يَأۡتِيَ يَوۡمࣱ لَّا مَرَدَّ لَهُۥ مِنَ ٱللَّهِۖ يَوۡمَئِذࣲ يَصَّدَّعُونَ
30:43.en: So set thy purpose resolutely for the right religion, before the inevitable day cometh from Allah. On that day mankind will be sundered

30:44.ar: مَن كَفَرَ فَعَلَيۡهِ كُفۡرُهُۥۖ وَمَنۡ عَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا فَلِأَنفُسِهِمۡ يَمۡهَدُونَ
30:44.en: Whoso disbelieveth must (then) bear the consequences of his disbelief, while those who do right make provision for themselves

30:45.ar: لِيَجۡزِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
30:45.en: That He may reward out of His bounty those who believe and do good works. Lo! He loveth not the disbelievers (in His guidance)

30:33.ar: وَإِذَا مَسَّ ٱلنَّاسَ ضُرࣱّ دَعَوۡاْ رَبَّهُم مُّنِيبِينَ إِلَيۡهِ ثُمَّ إِذَآ أَذَاقَهُم مِّنۡهُ رَحۡمَةً إِذَا فَرِيقࣱ مِّنۡهُم بِرَبِّهِمۡ يُشۡرِكُونَ
30:33.en: And when harm toucheth men they cry unto their Lord, turning to Him in repentance; then, when they have tasted of His mercy, behold! some of them attribute partners to their Lord

30:34.ar: لِيَكۡفُرُواْ بِمَآ ءَاتَيۡنَٰهُمۡۚ فَتَمَتَّعُواْ فَسَوۡفَ تَعۡلَمُونَ
30:34.en: So as to disbelieve in that which We have given them. (Unto such it is said): Enjoy yourselves awhile, but ye will come to know

30:35.ar: أَمۡ أَنزَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ سُلۡطَٰنࣰ ا فَهُوَ يَتَكَلَّمُ بِمَا كَانُواْ بِهِۦ يُشۡرِكُونَ
30:35.en: Or have We revealed unto them any warrant which speaketh of that which they associate with Him

30:36.ar: وَإِذَآ أَذَقۡنَا ٱلنَّاسَ رَحۡمَةࣰ فَرِحُواْ بِهَاۖ وَإِن تُصِبۡهُمۡ سَيِّئَةُۢ بِمَا قَدَّمَتۡ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ إِذَا هُمۡ يَقۡنَطُونَ
30:36.en: And when We cause mankind to taste of mercy they rejoice therein; but if an evil thing befall them as the consequence of their own deeds, lo! they are in despair

30:37.ar: أَوَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَبۡسُطُ ٱلرِّزۡقَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيَقۡدِرُۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يُؤۡمِنُونَ
30:37.en: See they not that Allah enlargeth the provision for whom He will, and straiteneth (it for whom He will). Lo! herein indeed are portents for folk who believe

30:38.ar: فَـَٔاتِ ذَا ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ حَقَّهُۥ وَٱلۡمِسۡكِينَ وَٱبۡنَ ٱلسَّبِيلِۚ ذَٰلِكَ خَيۡرࣱ لِّلَّذِينَ يُرِيدُونَ وَجۡهَ ٱللَّهِۖ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
30:38.en: So give to the kinsman his due, and to the needy, and to the wayfarer. That is best for those who seek Allah's Countenance. And such are they who are successful

30:39.ar: وَمَآ ءَاتَيۡتُم مِّن رِّبࣰ ا لِّيَرۡبُوَاْ فِيٓ أَمۡوَٰلِ ٱلنَّاسِ فَلَا يَرۡبُواْ عِندَ ٱللَّهِۖ وَمَآ ءَاتَيۡتُم مِّن زَكَوٰةࣲ تُرِيدُونَ وَجۡهَ ٱللَّهِ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُضۡعِفُونَ
30:39.en: That which ye give in usury in order that it may increase on (other) people's property hath no increase with Allah; but that which ye give in charity, seeking Allah's Countenance, hath increase manifold

30:20.ar: وَمِنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦٓ أَنۡ خَلَقَكُم مِّن تُرَابࣲ ثُمَّ إِذَآ أَنتُم بَشَرࣱ تَنتَشِرُونَ
30:20.en: And of His signs is this: He created you of dust, and behold you human beings, ranging widely

30:22.ar: وَمِنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ خَلۡقُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱخۡتِلَٰفُ أَلۡسِنَتِكُمۡ وَأَلۡوَٰنِكُمۡۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّلۡعَٰلِمِينَ
30:22.en: And of His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the difference of your languages and colours. Lo! herein indeed are portents for men of knowledge

35:28.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَٱلدَّوَآبِّ وَٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمِ مُخۡتَلِفٌ أَلۡوَٰنُهُۥ كَذَٰلِكَۗ إِنَّمَا يَخۡشَى ٱللَّهَ مِنۡ عِبَادِهِ ٱلۡعُلَمَٰٓؤُاْۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ غَفُورٌ
35:28.en: And of men and beasts and cattle, in like manner, divers hues? The erudite among His bondmen fear Allah alone. Lo! Allah is Mighty, Forgiving

30:54.ar: ۞ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكُم مِّن ضَعۡفࣲ ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ضَعۡفࣲ قُوَّةࣰ ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ قُوَّةࣲ ضَعۡفࣰ ا وَشَيۡبَةࣰۚ يَخۡلُقُ مَا يَشَآءُۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ ٱلۡقَدِيرُ
30:54.en: Allah is He Who shaped you out of weakness, then appointed after weakness strength, then, after strength, appointed weakness and grey hair. He createth what He will. He is the Knower, the Mighty

30:48.ar: ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي يُرۡسِلُ ٱلرِّيَٰحَ فَتُثِيرُ سَحَابࣰ ا فَيَبۡسُطُهُۥ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ كَيۡفَ يَشَآءُ وَيَجۡعَلُهُۥ كِسَفࣰ ا فَتَرَى ٱلۡوَدۡقَ يَخۡرُجُ مِنۡ خِلَٰلِهِۦۖ فَإِذَآ أَصَابَ بِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُ مِنۡ عِبَادِهِۦٓ إِذَا هُمۡ يَسۡتَبۡشِرُونَ
30:48.en: Allah is He Who sendeth the winds so that they raise clouds, and spreadeth them along the sky as pleaseth Him, and causeth them to break and thou seest the rain downpouring from within them. And when He maketh it to fall on whom He will of His bondmen, lo! they rejoice

29:20.ar: قُلۡ سِيرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَٱنظُرُواْ كَيۡفَ بَدَأَ ٱلۡخَلۡقَۚ ثُمَّ ٱللَّهُ يُنشِئُ ٱلنَّشۡأَةَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
29:20.en: Say (O Muhammad): Travel in the land and see how He originated creation, then Allah bringeth forth the later growth. Lo! Allah is Able to do all things

2:258.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِي حَآجَّ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ فِي رَبِّهِۦٓ أَنۡ ءَاتَىٰهُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُلۡكَ إِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّيَ ٱلَّذِي يُحۡيِۦ وَيُمِيتُ قَالَ أَنَا۠ أُحۡيِۦ وَأُمِيتُۖ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأۡتِي بِٱلشَّمۡسِ مِنَ ٱلۡمَشۡرِقِ فَأۡتِ بِهَا مِنَ ٱلۡمَغۡرِبِ فَبُهِتَ ٱلَّذِي كَفَرَۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
2:258.en: Bethink thee of him who had an argument with Abraham about his Lord, because Allah had given him the kingdom; how, when Abraham said: My Lord is He Who giveth life and causeth death, he answered: I give life and cause death. Abraham said: Lo! Allah causeth the sun to rise in the East, so do thou cause it to come up from the West. Thus was the disbeliever abashed. And Allah guideth not wrongdoing folk

7:56.ar: وَلَا تُفۡسِدُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ بَعۡدَ إِصۡلَٰحِهَا وَٱدۡعُوهُ خَوۡفࣰ ا وَطَمَعًاۚ إِنَّ رَحۡمَتَ ٱللَّهِ قَرِيبࣱ مِّنَ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
7:56.en: Work not confusion in the earth after the fair ordering (thereof). and call on Him in fear and hope. Lo! the mercy of Allah is nigh unto the good

7:31.ar: ۞يَٰبَنِيٓ ءَادَمَ خُذُواْ زِينَتَكُمۡ عِندَ كُلِّ مَسۡجِدࣲ وَكُلُواْ وَٱشۡرَبُواْ وَلَا تُسۡرِفُوٓاْۚ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُسۡرِفِينَ
7:31.en: O Children of Adam! Look to your adornment at every place of worship, and eat and drink, but be not prodigal. Lo! He loveth not the prodigals

7:164.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَتۡ أُمَّةࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡ لِمَ تَعِظُونَ قَوۡمًا ٱللَّهُ مُهۡلِكُهُمۡ أَوۡ مُعَذِّبُهُمۡ عَذَابࣰ ا شَدِيدࣰ اۖ قَالُواْ مَعۡذِرَةً إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُمۡ وَلَعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَّقُونَ
7:164.en: And when a community among them said: Why preach ye to a folk whom Allah is about to destroy or punish with an awful doom, they said: In order to be free from guilt before your Lord, and that haply they may ward off (evil)

30:30.ar: فَأَقِمۡ وَجۡهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفࣰ اۚ فِطۡرَتَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِي فَطَرَ ٱلنَّاسَ عَلَيۡهَاۚ لَا تَبۡدِيلَ لِخَلۡقِ ٱللَّهِۚ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلۡقَيِّمُ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
30:30.en: So set thy purpose (O Muhammad) for religion as a man by nature upright - the nature (framed) of Allah, in which He hath created man. There is no altering (the laws of) Allah's creation. That is the right religion, but most men know not

kCp23X1ADLw.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat Ar-Rum (Verses 40-45)
kCp23X1ADLw.one_line: Allah's laws in creation: science as discovering them, creation-provision-death-resurrection, and corruption on land and sea as the earned consequence of human choices.
kCp23X1ADLw.summary: He explains why he lingers on Ar-Rum: it is about Allah's laws in the universe, and a community that disrespects them cannot advance. Scientific laws discovered by others are Allah's own laws, so Muslims who oppose scientific theories in the name of Islam misunderstand both; the Quran is a book of law and values, science explains how, and knowing how deepens reverence. Historically, Muslim scholars were polymaths and conflict with science came only in the age of decline. Verse 40 lists four acts no partner can do: creating, providing, causing death and reviving; people accept the first three and deny the fourth, and Muslims glorify Allah rather than blaming Him in calamity. Verse 41 is his focus: fasad is any system failing its purpose, and it appears on land and sea through what people earn. Nothing done disappears: tyranny returns on tyrants, burning fuel heats the planet, and waste poisons the oceans. Allah lets people taste some consequences so they return, a deterrent most people need more than morals. He offers a rule: act in a way that would set the world right if everyone did it, and claim no exceptions. He ends by urging Muslims to learn from their own history.

outline.heading: Why he lingers on this surah
outline.gist: Understanding Allah's laws in the universe shapes the present and future of the community.

outline.heading: A community that ignores Allah's laws cannot advance
outline.gist: Wanting provision without effort defies a basic law; Muslims withdrew from science for centuries while others led.

outline.heading: The false split between scientific and Quranic laws
outline.gist: Muslims came to see discovered laws as 'theirs' and separate from the Quran's.

outline.heading: Discovered laws are Allah's laws
outline.gist: Allah created gravity, electromagnetism and causality; honouring these laws is part of revering Him, and Ar-Rum lists such signs.

outline.heading: Diversity and a round earth are His creation
outline.gist: Languages, colours and the shape of the earth are His design and do not threaten Islam.

outline.heading: Opposing scientific theories in Islam's name
outline.gist: Science may err and correct itself, but in the end it explains how Allah made things; the Quran does not address the how.

outline.heading: The Quran is a book of law and values
outline.gist: It is not a biology text; Muslims were lost only when they stopped reading and discovering.

outline.heading: Respect the laws and benefit; defy them and be destroyed
outline.gist: No one overpowers Allah's laws; nature with its pain and beauty was made for us to learn from.

outline.heading: Islam and science never conflicted
outline.gist: Other religions fought science; the Arabs had wisdom not sciences, and scholarship flourished wherever Islam spread.

outline.heading: Scholars were polymaths
outline.gist: His khutbah challenge from Siyar A'lam al-Nubala: most scholars sampled also mastered medicine, botany or languages; al-Suyuti on mathematics.

outline.heading: Conflict came with decline
outline.gist: Hostility to science arose late in the Ottoman era; our history has bright and dark pages.

outline.heading: Every science points to Allah
outline.gist: A student fearing for his faith should know that understanding how deepens reverence, as with the cell's signalling pathways.

outline.heading: Islam as the religion of nature
outline.gist: Islam respects the nature of men, women, children and societies; he will summarise the surah's laws at the end.

outline.heading: Verses that begin with Allah's name
outline.gist: Several verses of Ar-Rum open with 'Allah is the One who', because every law listed comes from Him.

outline.heading: Discoveries should lead to glorification
outline.gist: The West strips discoveries of Allah, but a Muslim finding a new gene or planet should praise the Creator.

outline.heading: Recitation of verses 40-41
outline.gist: Recitation of the verses on creating, providing, death and life, and corruption on land and sea.

outline.heading: Recap: how to deal with harm and mercy
outline.gist: Last week's verses on human reactions to hardship and mercy and on giving relatives their due.

outline.heading: First law: He created you
outline.gist: If you did not bring yourself into being, you are created; there is no middle between creator and created.

outline.heading: Awareness comes late
outline.gist: Human consciousness opens around twelve; we remember fragments of childhood and are not held accountable for it.

outline.heading: Who created and how
outline.gist: Science answers how creation began, as Allah commands; the verse tells us who.

outline.heading: Second law: an allotted provision
outline.gist: Each person has a set portion of food, drink and deeds, expanded or restricted.

outline.heading: Death, then being brought back to life
outline.gist: People accept creation, provision and death as shared by all, yet deny being revived.

outline.heading: Ibrahim and the king who claimed to give life
outline.gist: Killing one man and sparing another is not giving life; Ibrahim moved to the sun rising in the east.

outline.heading: Can any partner do any of this?
outline.gist: These are glorifying verses describing acts Allah alone performs.

outline.heading: Tasbih is a Muslim trait
outline.gist: Glorifying Allah means refusing to attribute any defect or fault to Him.

outline.heading: Do not blame Allah in calamity
outline.gist: The soul wants to shift blame to a higher power during wars and famines; a Muslim glorifies Him instead.

outline.heading: Other faiths attribute error to God
outline.gist: Many believers in other religions ascribe mistakes, neglect and forgetfulness to God.

outline.heading: What fasad means
outline.gist: Corruption is any system failing its purpose, as spoiled food no longer feeds people though it makes good fertiliser.

outline.heading: Prophets forbade corruption in the land
outline.gist: The word unites the physical, intellectual and behavioural; every prophet warned against it.

outline.heading: Corruption in the sea in the Prophet's time?
outline.gist: Classical explanations did not satisfy him; the companions accepted the verse without forced readings.

outline.heading: What people's hands earn
outline.gist: Allah creates acts and people choose them; like the butterfly effect, a wrong never vanishes and only justice fixes it.

outline.heading: Oppression returns like a boomerang
outline.gist: The Russian revolution killed the tyrant monarchy's children; al-Shafi'i's verse that whoever violates others' honour is repaid.

outline.heading: A law others call karma
outline.gist: You cannot spread harm without paying for it; people inferred this law from observation.

outline.heading: Burning the planet
outline.gist: Overproduction and burning fuel have heated the earth beyond return; heatwaves, dry springs, and a pandemic that shut the world economy.

outline.heading: Neither good nor evil disappears
outline.gist: Uprightness and corruption both spread and remain.

outline.heading: Tasting consequences deters
outline.gist: Few refrain for moral reasons; consequences hold people back so that they return, so cut needless consumption.

outline.heading: Shame and the ongoing past tense
outline.gist: Most avoid sin for fear of exposure; the past tense describes corruption that keeps appearing while people earn it.

outline.heading: You have real influence on the earth
outline.gist: As those who warned the Sabbath-breakers did, we warn so people may return; Allah could have made us powerless but did not.

outline.heading: Our corruption reaches the oceans
outline.gist: Rubbish and carcinogens spread through seas we have barely explored, and the harm returns on people.

outline.heading: Negative reinforcement
outline.gist: If wrongdoing brought good results people would do more; bad consequences stop them, then morals follow.

outline.heading: Live as if everyone lived like you
outline.gist: His rule: if your conduct, copied by all, would fix the world, continue; if it would ruin it, you are the corrupter.

outline.heading: No one has an exception
outline.gist: Cheating the government or one's job 'just this once' would ruin the earth if all did it; one verse covers act, consequence, cause and purpose.

outline.heading: Recitation of verses 42-45
outline.gist: Travel the earth and see the end of those before; set your face to the upright religion before the Day.

outline.heading: Recap and the command to travel and observe
outline.gist: The Quran repeatedly commands travelling to see what became of earlier corrupters.

outline.heading: Learn from our own history
outline.gist: How did Muslims go from a caliphate spanning three continents to their present state?

outline.heading: Most of them were associators
outline.gist: Shirk lets people grant themselves permission for corruption Allah forbade.

outline.heading: The upright religion, twice in Ar-Rum
outline.gist: Set your face to the religion of fitrah, and to the religion that upholds values: both phrasings occur only in this surah.

30:30.ar: فَأَقِمۡ وَجۡهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفࣰ اۚ فِطۡرَتَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِي فَطَرَ ٱلنَّاسَ عَلَيۡهَاۚ لَا تَبۡدِيلَ لِخَلۡقِ ٱللَّهِۚ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلۡقَيِّمُ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
30:30.en: So set thy purpose (O Muhammad) for religion as a man by nature upright - the nature (framed) of Allah, in which He hath created man. There is no altering (the laws of) Allah's creation. That is the right religion, but most men know not

30:31.ar: ۞مُنِيبِينَ إِلَيۡهِ وَٱتَّقُوهُ وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَلَا تَكُونُواْ مِنَ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ
30:31.en: Turning unto Him (only); and be careful of your duty unto Him and establish worship, and be not of those who ascribe partners (unto Him)

30:32.ar: مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ فَرَّقُواْ دِينَهُمۡ وَكَانُواْ شِيَعࣰ اۖ كُلُّ حِزۡبِۭ بِمَا لَدَيۡهِمۡ فَرِحُونَ
30:32.en: Of those who split up their religion and became schismatics, each sect exulting in its tenets

30:33.ar: وَإِذَا مَسَّ ٱلنَّاسَ ضُرࣱّ دَعَوۡاْ رَبَّهُم مُّنِيبِينَ إِلَيۡهِ ثُمَّ إِذَآ أَذَاقَهُم مِّنۡهُ رَحۡمَةً إِذَا فَرِيقࣱ مِّنۡهُم بِرَبِّهِمۡ يُشۡرِكُونَ
30:33.en: And when harm toucheth men they cry unto their Lord, turning to Him in repentance; then, when they have tasted of His mercy, behold! some of them attribute partners to their Lord

30:34.ar: لِيَكۡفُرُواْ بِمَآ ءَاتَيۡنَٰهُمۡۚ فَتَمَتَّعُواْ فَسَوۡفَ تَعۡلَمُونَ
30:34.en: So as to disbelieve in that which We have given them. (Unto such it is said): Enjoy yourselves awhile, but ye will come to know

30:35.ar: أَمۡ أَنزَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ سُلۡطَٰنࣰ ا فَهُوَ يَتَكَلَّمُ بِمَا كَانُواْ بِهِۦ يُشۡرِكُونَ
30:35.en: Or have We revealed unto them any warrant which speaketh of that which they associate with Him

30:36.ar: وَإِذَآ أَذَقۡنَا ٱلنَّاسَ رَحۡمَةࣰ فَرِحُواْ بِهَاۖ وَإِن تُصِبۡهُمۡ سَيِّئَةُۢ بِمَا قَدَّمَتۡ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ إِذَا هُمۡ يَقۡنَطُونَ
30:36.en: And when We cause mankind to taste of mercy they rejoice therein; but if an evil thing befall them as the consequence of their own deeds, lo! they are in despair

30:37.ar: أَوَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَبۡسُطُ ٱلرِّزۡقَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيَقۡدِرُۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يُؤۡمِنُونَ
30:37.en: See they not that Allah enlargeth the provision for whom He will, and straiteneth (it for whom He will). Lo! herein indeed are portents for folk who believe

30:38.ar: فَـَٔاتِ ذَا ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ حَقَّهُۥ وَٱلۡمِسۡكِينَ وَٱبۡنَ ٱلسَّبِيلِۚ ذَٰلِكَ خَيۡرࣱ لِّلَّذِينَ يُرِيدُونَ وَجۡهَ ٱللَّهِۖ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
30:38.en: So give to the kinsman his due, and to the needy, and to the wayfarer. That is best for those who seek Allah's Countenance. And such are they who are successful

30:39.ar: وَمَآ ءَاتَيۡتُم مِّن رِّبࣰ ا لِّيَرۡبُوَاْ فِيٓ أَمۡوَٰلِ ٱلنَّاسِ فَلَا يَرۡبُواْ عِندَ ٱللَّهِۖ وَمَآ ءَاتَيۡتُم مِّن زَكَوٰةࣲ تُرِيدُونَ وَجۡهَ ٱللَّهِ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُضۡعِفُونَ
30:39.en: That which ye give in usury in order that it may increase on (other) people's property hath no increase with Allah; but that which ye give in charity, seeking Allah's Countenance, hath increase manifold

95:4.ar: لَقَدۡ خَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ فِيٓ أَحۡسَنِ تَقۡوِيمࣲ‏
95:4.en: Surely We created man of the best stature

95:5.en: Then we reduced him to the lowest of the low

4:46.ar: مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ يُحَرِّفُونَ ٱلۡكَلِمَ عَن مَّوَاضِعِهِۦ وَيَقُولُونَ سَمِعۡنَا وَعَصَيۡنَا وَٱسۡمَعۡ غَيۡرَ مُسۡمَعࣲ وَرَٰعِنَا لَيَّۢا بِأَلۡسِنَتِهِمۡ وَطَعۡنࣰ ا فِي ٱلدِّينِۚ وَلَوۡ أَنَّهُمۡ قَالُواْ سَمِعۡنَا وَأَطَعۡنَا وَٱسۡمَعۡ وَٱنظُرۡنَا لَكَانَ خَيۡرࣰ ا لَّهُمۡ وَأَقۡوَمَ وَلَٰكِن لَّعَنَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُفۡرِهِمۡ فَلَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ ا
4:46.en: Some of those who are Jews change words from their context and say: "We hear and disobey; hear thou as one who heareth not" and "Listen to us!" distorting with their tongues and slandering religion. If they had said: "We hear and we obey: hear thou, and look at us" it had been better for them, and more upright. But Allah hath cursed them for their disbelief, so they believe not, save a few

2:275.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَأۡكُلُونَ ٱلرِّبَوٰاْ لَا يَقُومُونَ إِلَّا كَمَا يَقُومُ ٱلَّذِي يَتَخَبَّطُهُ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ مِنَ ٱلۡمَسِّۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّمَا ٱلۡبَيۡعُ مِثۡلُ ٱلرِّبَوٰاْۗ وَأَحَلَّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡبَيۡعَ وَحَرَّمَ ٱلرِّبَوٰاْۚ فَمَن جَآءَهُۥ مَوۡعِظَةࣱ مِّن رَّبِّهِۦ فَٱنتَهَىٰ فَلَهُۥ مَا سَلَفَ وَأَمۡرُهُۥٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِۖ وَمَنۡ عَادَ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلنَّارِۖ هُمۡ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
2:275.en: Those who swallow usury cannot rise up save as he ariseth whom the devil hath prostrated by (his) touch. That is because they say: Trade is just like usury; whereas Allah permitteth trading and forbiddeth usury. He unto whom an admonition from his Lord cometh, and (he) refraineth (in obedience thereto), he shall keep (the profits of) that which is past, and his affair (henceforth) is with Allah. As for him who returneth (to usury) - Such are rightful owners of the Fire. They will abide therein

4:76.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ يُقَٰتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۖ وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ يُقَٰتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱلطَّٰغُوتِ فَقَٰتِلُوٓاْ أَوۡلِيَآءَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِۖ إِنَّ كَيۡدَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ كَانَ ضَعِيفًا
4:76.en: Those who believe do battle for the cause of Allah; and those who disbelieve do battle for the cause of idols. So fight the minions of the devil. Lo! the devil's strategy is ever weak

10:58.ar: قُلۡ بِفَضۡلِ ٱللَّهِ وَبِرَحۡمَتِهِۦ فَبِذَٰلِكَ فَلۡيَفۡرَحُواْ هُوَ خَيۡرࣱ مِّمَّا يَجۡمَعُونَ
10:58.en: Say: In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy: therein let them rejoice. It is better than what they hoard

28:76.ar: ۞إِنَّ قَٰرُونَ كَانَ مِن قَوۡمِ مُوسَىٰ فَبَغَىٰ عَلَيۡهِمۡۖ وَءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلۡكُنُوزِ مَآ إِنَّ مَفَاتِحَهُۥ لَتَنُوٓأُ بِٱلۡعُصۡبَةِ أُوْلِي ٱلۡقُوَّةِ إِذۡ قَالَ لَهُۥ قَوۡمُهُۥ لَا تَفۡرَحۡۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡفَرِحِينَ
28:76.en: Now Korah was of Moses' folk, but he oppressed them; and We gave him so much treasure that the stores thereof would verily have been a burden for a troop of mighty men. When his own folk said unto him: Exult not; lo! Allah loveth not the exultant

15:56.ar: قَالَ وَمَن يَقۡنَطُ مِن رَّحۡمَةِ رَبِّهِۦٓ إِلَّا ٱلضَّآلُّونَ
15:56.en: He said: And who despaireth of the mercy of his Lord save those who are astray

12:87.ar: يَٰبَنِيَّ ٱذۡهَبُواْ فَتَحَسَّسُواْ مِن يُوسُفَ وَأَخِيهِ وَلَا تَاْيۡـَٔسُواْ مِن رَّوۡحِ ٱللَّهِۖ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يَاْيۡـَٔسُ مِن رَّوۡحِ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلۡقَوۡمُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ
12:87.en: Go, O my sons, and ascertain concerning Joseph and his brother, and despair not of the Spirit of Allah. Lo! none despaireth of the Spirit of Allah save disbelieving folk

89:16.ar: وَأَمَّآ إِذَا مَا ٱبۡتَلَىٰهُ فَقَدَرَ عَلَيۡهِ رِزۡقَهُۥ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّيٓ أَهَٰنَنِ
89:16.en: But whenever He trieth him by straitening his means of life, he saith: My Lord despiseth me

21:87.ar: وَذَا ٱلنُّونِ إِذ ذَّهَبَ مُغَٰضِبࣰ ا فَظَنَّ أَن لَّن نَّقۡدِرَ عَلَيۡهِ فَنَادَىٰ فِي ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ أَن لَّآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنتَ سُبۡحَٰنَكَ إِنِّي كُنتُ مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
21:87.en: And (mention) Dhu'n-Nun, when he went off in anger and deemed that We had no power over him, but he cried out in the darkness, saying: There is no Allah save Thee. Be Thou Glorified! Lo! I have been a wrong-doer

7:157.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ ٱلرَّسُولَ ٱلنَّبِيَّ ٱلۡأُمِّيَّ ٱلَّذِي يَجِدُونَهُۥ مَكۡتُوبًا عِندَهُمۡ فِي ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةِ وَٱلۡإِنجِيلِ يَأۡمُرُهُم بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ وَيَنۡهَىٰهُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡمُنكَرِ وَيُحِلُّ لَهُمُ ٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ وَيُحَرِّمُ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡخَبَٰٓئِثَ وَيَضَعُ عَنۡهُمۡ إِصۡرَهُمۡ وَٱلۡأَغۡلَٰلَ ٱلَّتِي كَانَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمۡۚ فَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ بِهِۦ وَعَزَّرُوهُ وَنَصَرُوهُ وَٱتَّبَعُواْ ٱلنُّورَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أُنزِلَ مَعَهُۥٓ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
7:157.en: Those who follow the messenger, the Prophet who can neither read nor write, whom they will find described in the Torah and the Gospel (which are) with them. He will enjoin on them that which is right and forbid them that which is wrong. He will make lawful for them all good things and prohibit for them only the foul; and he will relieve them of their burden and the fetters that they used to wear. Then those who believe in him, and honour him, and help him, and follow the light which is sent down with him: they are the successful

58:1.ar: قَدۡ سَمِعَ ٱللَّهُ قَوۡلَ ٱلَّتِي تُجَٰدِلُكَ فِي زَوۡجِهَا وَتَشۡتَكِيٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَٱللَّهُ يَسۡمَعُ تَحَاوُرَكُمَآۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَمِيعُۢ بَصِيرٌ
58:1.en: Allah hath heard the saying of her that disputeth with thee (Muhammad) concerning her husband, and complaineth unto Allah. And Allah heareth your colloquy. Lo! Allah is Hearer, Knower

3:130.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَأۡكُلُواْ ٱلرِّبَوٰٓاْ أَضۡعَٰفࣰ ا مُّضَٰعَفَةࣰۖ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ
3:130.en: O ye who believe! Devour not usury, doubling and quadrupling (the sum lent). Observe your duty to Allah, that ye may be successful

2:276.ar: يَمۡحَقُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلرِّبَوٰاْ وَيُرۡبِي ٱلصَّدَقَٰتِۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ كَفَّارٍ أَثِيمٍ
2:276.en: Allah hath blighted usury and made almsgiving fruitful. Allah loveth not the impious and guilty

xOjBXaK3ntQ.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat Ar-Rum (30:30-39)
xOjBXaK3ntQ.one_line: Islam fits human nature; how people mishandle harm and mercy, why both wealth and want are tests, and riba versus giving for Allah's face.
xOjBXaK3ntQ.summary: He recaps the surah's theme: Allah's laws, called ayat, govern nature, the self and our relationship with Him. Islam is the religion of fitrah, made to fit human nature and lift it; sects arose when people tailored the religion to their desires instead of changing themselves to fit it. Verses 33 to 36 describe a recurring human pattern. When a little harm touches people they turn to Allah in repentance, as even atheists do, then once mercy comes some credit others with it. That shirk creates worldly loyalties and ends in ingratitude, while seeing every gift, spouse and child as a trust from Allah keeps you grateful. Others become arrogant in good times and despair when they suffer for their own mistakes. Neither reaction has any authority behind it. Verses 37 to 39 give the remedy: Allah expands and restricts provision, and both are tests. Some moments of joy will be regretted on the Day of Judgment, and some calamities will be the best hours of a life. Those who seek Allah's face focus on what they owe, giving relatives, the poor and travellers their rights. Riba, known as evil even before its ban, grows wealth among people but not with Allah, while charity is multiplied. He urges people living amid blessings to complain less.

outline.heading: Ar-Rum: humans and Allah's laws
outline.gist: The Quran calls these laws ayat: in nature, in the self and in our relationship with Allah.

outline.heading: Islam is the religion of fitrah
outline.gist: Its commands fit human nature and help it rise; a person can move up or sink to the lowest of the low.

outline.heading: Hanif, unchanging creation, the upright religion
outline.gist: All people share one fitrah; al-qayyim and taqwim share a root: fit for the mission you were given.

outline.heading: Sects: tailoring the religion to yourself
outline.gist: Splinter groups changed the shari'ah to suit desires; change yourself to fit Islam, not Islam to fit you.

outline.heading: Examples of groups that left the mainstream
outline.gist: Those who wanted continued revelation after the Prophet, the Qadariyyah and the Jabriyyah each rejected part of the fitrah.

outline.heading: Personal versions of Islam and bargain-hunting fatwas
outline.gist: Admitting you cannot yet live up to a command is fine; seeking discounts on clear prohibitions is not.

outline.heading: A religion fitted to us and our world
outline.gist: The coming verses describe parts of human nature we can refine but not change.

outline.heading: Reciting 30:33-36 and the light lam of 'sultan'
outline.gist: The verses set out two scenarios: harm followed by mercy, and mercy followed by harm.

outline.heading: Harm, not evil, and the meaning of mass
outline.gist: Allah sends harm whose outcome depends on your response; mass is the lightest touch.

outline.heading: Shaytan touches; he does not possess
outline.gist: His mass is a whisper that clouds your clarity; his scheming is weak, so the notion of possession does not fit.

outline.heading: Small harm reveals our weakness
outline.gist: A headache or a toe ache makes a person turn to a higher power; this is fitrah, even in atheists.

outline.heading: After mercy, shirk as partnership and interest
outline.gist: Crediting others with Allah's gift creates worldly loyalties; tawhid removes those interests.

outline.heading: Shirk ends in ingratitude
outline.gist: A gift seen as from a person soon bores you; seen as from Allah you stay grateful to Him and to the giver.

outline.heading: Spouses and children as trusts from Allah
outline.gist: Seeing everything as a trust keeps you patient and content; otherwise you tire of it.

outline.heading: 'Enjoy, you will come to know' and 'have We sent them authority?'
outline.gist: A mocking question: no proof tells them to behave this way.

outline.heading: The cycle repeats throughout life
outline.gist: You beg for a job, then curse it two years later; the gratitude of the moment of relief fades.

outline.heading: No basis for how you handle harm and mercy
outline.gist: A law that recurs a thousand times in your life cannot be met with a method from your own head.

outline.heading: Al-Muhallabi: 'is there no death for sale?'
outline.gist: A man in despair was helped, rose to be vizier, and had to be reminded of those days.

outline.heading: Second scenario: farah as arrogance
outline.gist: In the Quran farah usually means the conceited joy of one who credits himself, as with Qarun.

outline.heading: Despair after self-earned harm
outline.gist: Qunut is extreme hopelessness; yesterday on the hilltop, today wanting to die.

outline.heading: The law of alternation
outline.gist: Harm and mercy succeed each other for everyone; ask anyone who lived long.

outline.heading: Reciting 30:37-39
outline.gist: Note 'liyarbuwa' with fathah and 'yarbu' without.

outline.heading: Qadar means restriction: Ibn Abbas and Mu'awiyah on Yunus
outline.gist: Yunus thought Allah would not constrain him, not that Allah lacked power.

outline.heading: Plenty and scarcity are both tests
outline.gist: Neither means love or disgrace; you leave testing only on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: Joys regretted and calamities celebrated on the Last Day
outline.gist: The best hour of your life may become the worst, and a patient calamity may raise you and let you intercede for your family.

outline.heading: Give relatives, the poor and travellers their rights
outline.gist: Whether you have much or little, give of your money, time and care.

outline.heading: Seeking the face of Allah
outline.gist: To want to be in His presence on the Last Day; set your face to the religion and He receives you with His face.

outline.heading: The highest in Paradise look at His face
outline.gist: They wait between one sight and the next, wanting nothing else.

outline.heading: Focus on what you owe, not on what you get
outline.gist: The successful treat giving and withholding alike as tests and fulfil their duties.

outline.heading: Complain less
outline.gist: We live surrounded by mercy; be ashamed to complain and help those whose blood and land were taken.

outline.heading: Riba was known as evil before its ban
outline.gist: A Meccan surah, before the decisive prohibition; every people knew riba is ugly.

outline.heading: Khawlah's dispute and Quraysh's clean money for the Kaaba
outline.gist: People sensed what the religion of fitrah would forbid; Quraysh refused riba money in rebuilding the Kaaba.

outline.heading: You already know the right answer
outline.gist: Most people asking for a fatwa know what they should do; he will not carry their choice for them.

outline.heading: Riba grows among people, zakat grows with Allah
outline.gist: Wealth multiplied by riba does not increase with Allah; those who give for His face are the multipliers.

outline.heading: Lending to Allah
outline.gist: Allah blots out riba and grows charity, raising a small gift like a foal into a mountain.

outline.heading: Choose how you meet harm and mercy
outline.gist: Despair, conceit and shirk, or giving people their rights for Allah's face.

outline.heading: Outro
